title: NP search relative to an oracle

problem.name: Oracle-verifier search
problem.statement_latex: Given oracle access to a predicate $V(x,w)$ with $w\in\{0,1\}^n$, decide whether $\exists w\,V(x,w)=1$ and return such a witness when one exists, with probability at least $2/3$. This abstracts verifier access in SAT, exact cover and NP optimization decision problems. Complexity is measured in verifier-oracle queries; the explicit-circuit variant additionally uses classical bit-operation time.
problem.statement_text: Given oracle access to a predicate $V(x,w)$ with $w\in\{0,1\}^n$, decide whether $\exists w\,V(x,w)=1$ and return such a witness when one exists, with probability at least $2/3$. This abstracts verifier access in SAT, exact cover and NP optimization decision problems. Complexity is measured in verifier-oracle queries; the explicit-circuit variant additionally uses classical bit-operation time.

quantum.details_latex: This is the optimal worst-case bound for arbitrary verifier access. Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard and Vazirani prove that, relative to a random oracle with probability one, quantum time $o(2^{n/2})$ cannot contain NP in their oracle formulation.
quantum.details_text: This is the optimal worst-case bound for arbitrary verifier access. Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard and Vazirani prove that, relative to a random oracle with probability one, quantum time $o(2^{n/2})$ cannot contain NP in their oracle formulation.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(2^n)$ verifier queries, exhaustive or randomized witness search.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(2^n)$ verifier queries, exhaustive or randomized witness search.
classical.details_latex:
For an explicitly given bounded-fan-in verifier with $g$ gates, a count-preserving Tseitin encoding has $O(n+g)$ variables and clauses. Sparse fixed-width counting then gives witness search in
\[
\operatorname{poly}(n+g)2^{O((n+g)/\sqrt{\log(n+g)})}.
\]
A linear-size verifier therefore has a subexponential classical search algorithm. In the ordinary circuit model, a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for an NP-complete problem would imply $\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}$.

strength.description_latex: Tight square-root improvement in the number of candidate witnesses. In witness length $n$, the oracle comparison improves the exponential constant without power saving.
strength.description_text: Tight square-root improvement in the number of candidate witnesses. In witness length $n$, the oracle comparison improves the exponential constant without power saving.

evidence.description_latex: Fully rigorous for oracle-verifier access; the explicit-circuit upper bound uses the supplied circuit structure.

hardware.description_latex: The search kernel needs $n$ witness qubits plus a reversible verifier's ancillas. Exponentially many coherent iterations require fault-tolerant execution at large instance sizes.
